instruction: In the best_awards_acl.xlsx file on the desktop, add borders to all cells in the table range A1:D2 to make the table structure more visible.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding borders to all cells in the range A1:D2. The evaluator checks if all cells in this range have at least one border side set.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts border state from all cells in range A1:D2 using openpyxl
Getter properly checks if each cell has at least one border side with a style set (left/right/top/bottom)
Metric correctly compares boolean result against expected value (has_borders: true)
Complete coverage: evaluator checks ALL cells in the required range A1:D2
Postconfig appropriately saves the file with Ctrl+S to ensure border changes are persisted
Expected value is semantically correct for the task requirement
Data flow is correct: file download -> openpyxl parsing -> border checking -> boolean comparison
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The check 'if not cell.border:' on getter line 40 is redundant since openpyxl cell.border objects always exist. However, this doesn't affect correctness as the real validation happens in lines 43-48.

Consider: The getter checks for 'at least one border side' which is reasonable, but 'add borders to make table structure visible' might traditionally mean all four borders. Current implementation is acceptable but could be made more strict if needed.
